paragraphs: Speculative military design tends to converge on the same features: faceted armour to defeat sensors, a low profile because height is a liability, and wheels rather than tracks because most future conflicts in fiction happen on roads.

The model holds 308,070 polygons and 168,983 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. Rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D.
At $79 it suits science fiction film and animation, game vehicles and environments, concept art, defence and technology illustration, and advertising. On sale since 2024.

A golf bag is a portable rack with a strict order to it. Woods at the top where the long shafts have room, irons in the middle, putter wherever the owner has decided, and the whole arrangement is personal enough that players notice immediately when it is wrong.

The model holds 61,829 polygons and 62,054 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured generously with 51 maps at 2048x2048, and supplies the bag together with the clubs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits sports and equipment visualisation, retail and e-commerce imagery, advertising, club and course scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

The Hampshire is the pig with the white belt across black shoulders, and the marking breeds true, which is why it is one of the oldest recognisable breeds in America. A sow is the animal a farm is actually built around, since everything else on the unit descends from her.

The model is light at 16,029 polygons and 16,205 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 15 maps, 5 at 4096x4096, 5 at 2048x2048 and 5 at 1024x1024. It carries StemCell certification, and standing, walking and rigged builds are offered separately.
At $79 it suits agricultural and livestock visualisation, food industry presentation, education and documentary work, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The motel is a building type invented by the car. Doors that open onto the parking lot instead of a corridor, a single storey so nobody carries luggage upstairs, and a sign designed to be read at speed from a road that has no other reason to stop.
The model is light at 102,785 polygons and 110,856 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to wide roadside scenes. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits architectural and urban visualisation, film and television backgrounds, roadside and period scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A touring caravan is a house designed to be dragged. Every fitting has to survive being towed at motorway speed, every cupboard has to latch, and the whole interior is planned around a payload limit that most owners exceed on the first trip.

The model holds 77,634 polygons and 81,657 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 17 maps, 11 at 4096x4096 and 6 at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits leisure and tourism visualisation, vehicle and campsite scenes, advertising, architectural backgrounds, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2016.

A hopper wagon unloads by gravity through doors in its floor, which is why the body slopes inward from the top. Grain, coal and aggregate all move this way, and the whole design exists so that nobody has to climb inside to empty it.

The model holds 540,447 polygons and 556,630 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 9 maps all at 4096x4096, in a generic scheme carrying no markings. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a second build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits rail and freight visualisation, logistics and infrastructure presentation, industrial scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

Continuous welded rail has to be pulled into tension before the ends are joined, because steel that is laid slack in winter will buckle in summer. The puller is the machine that does that stretching, clamped to the rail itself.
The model holds 103,839 polygons and 107,128 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied mounted on track. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits railway engineering and maintenance visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, infrastructure presentation and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Hypersonic weapons are difficult less because of the speed than because of what the speed does: the air in front of the vehicle turns to plasma, the surface heats past what most materials tolerate, and steering has to happen in conditions where the sensors can barely see out.
The model holds 63,437 polygons and 63,757 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, science and technology illustration, and game environments. On sale since 2022.

Ceremonial guard uniform is a working combat dress from the nineteenth century that was never retired. The scarlet tunic, the bearskin and the placement of the buttons all carry regimental information, and the whole ensemble is maintained to a standard no field army could afford.
The uniform holds 27,706 polygons and 28,840 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits ceremonial and historical visualisation, film and television costume, tourism and editorial imagery, game characters and education material. On sale since 2017.

The PC-98 dominated Japan while the rest of the world standardised on something else entirely, largely because handling Japanese text needed hardware that western machines did not have. An entire software culture grew up on it and stayed there for over a decade.
The model holds 214,940 polygons and 115,918 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is enough for close product and desk work. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits retro technology visualisation, period film and television, product and museum imagery, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A gi is cut deliberately loose and made deliberately heavy, because the fabric is part of the practice: it has to be grabbed, pulled and snapped without tearing, and the sound it makes on a properly executed technique is used as feedback in the dojo.
The uniform is light at 22,233 polygons and 11,252 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in blue, so it costs little in a scene. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits sports and martial arts visualisation, apparel and retail imagery, game characters, advertising, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Rice is planted, not sown, and for most of history that meant people bent double in water for weeks. A transplanter takes seedlings from a tray and pushes them into mud at the right depth and spacing, several rows at a time, from a machine light enough not to sink.
The model holds 221,073 polygons and 230,840 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, supplied in working position, and carries StemCell certification.
At $79 it suits agricultural machinery marketing, farming and agritech visualisation, education and documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The heavy payload arm is the one that lifts car bodies. Everything about it is scaled up from the familiar orange robot: thicker castings, larger bearings, and a reach that means the safety cage around it becomes a serious piece of engineering in itself.

The model holds 95,512 polygons and 95,089 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 64 maps, 32 at 4096x4096 and 32 at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits manufacturing and automation visualisation, robotics marketing, factory scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2016.

A mid range industrial arm is the workhorse of automation: big enough to handle a real part, small enough to fit in a cell beside a machine tool. Most of what robots actually do in factories happens at this size rather than at either extreme.

The model holds 223,520 polygons and 226,077 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 14 maps, 5 at 8192x8192, one at 4096x4096, 6 at 2048x2048 and 2 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits manufacturing and automation visualisation, robotics marketing, factory and workshop scenes, training material and game environments. On sale since 2016.
